github.title: Count a tab or pane that is gone at the close as closed in launcher stop
github.author: jerridan

identity.head: 475a6ec173af6d118a33c8a723d50c3fad8c3953
identity.description:
Count a tab or pane that is gone at the close as closed in launcher stop

## Summary

When an orchestrator closes an item, `launcher.py stop` types `/exit` into the implementer session and then closes its tab or pane. Sometimes the tab or pane closes by itself between the check that it exists and the close, and `stop` then exited 6 for a stop that worked. Now `stop` reads the tab or pane again when the close fails: when it is gone, the stop counts as done and exits 0. A failure on a tab or pane that still exists keeps exit 6 and its stderr line.

**Ticket:** N/A
**Type:** Bug fix

---

## Agent context

### Authority

`skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md` owns the interface of `launcher.py`, and its "focus and stop" section already said that a tab or pane that closed when `claude` ended is not an error.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/launcher.py`: tmux: when `kill-pane` fails, `stop` checks the pane again, and a pane that is gone is no failure. iTerm2: when the close script (`OSA_STOP`) or the exit script (`OSA_EXIT`) fails, the new `iterm_gone` reads the sessions, and a session that is gone is no failure. A failed read keeps the failure. Herdr: when `hc send /exit` fails, the new `hc_ended` reads `hc get`, and a terminal that is gone or not live is no failure: `stop` goes on and closes the tab. The close of a Herdr tab already read `herdr-app ls` after a failure.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-launcher.sh`: new stub switches `tmux-kill-gone`, `osa-stop-gone`, `osa-exit-gone`, `osa-stop-keep` and `hc-send-gone`, and five checks: four gone cases (tmux close, iTerm2 close, iTerm2 exit, Herdr `hc send`) and one iTerm2 close failure on a session that still exists, which exits 6.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md`: "focus and stop" says per terminal which failure counts as closed and which exits 6.

### Constraints that applied

- The plugin `version` is not bumped here. The orchestrator owns it and sets it when this PR is next to merge.
- No `docs/design.md` §15 entry: the orchestrator owns the numbers.

### How this was verified

`bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-launcher.sh`: 277 of 277 checks passed at the branch head. Before the fix, the new checks failed (273 of 277).

Which terminals had the race: tmux had it, as seen once on 0.1.118 (`kill-pane` failed with "can't find pane" and exit 6). iTerm2 can have it inside its close script and its exit script. Herdr's close already counted a gone tab as closed, and its shell stays open after `claude` ends, so its tab does not close by itself in normal use. Only `hc send` could fail for a terminal that ended during the send.

### Known gaps

No live run reproduced the race on any terminal. Only the stubbed test covers the timing.

## Charter

Goal: `launcher.py stop` reports success when the tab or pane closed by itself after `/exit`.

Acceptance criterion: `bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-launcher.sh` passes, and holds new checks that `stop` exits 0 with no stderr failure line when the tab or pane is gone at the close step, and that a close failure on a tab or pane that still exists keeps exit 6 and its stderr line.

## Decisions

- Which path does this goal take? The change path (precedent, high).
- Does the work take the light path? Yes: one package, a runnable criterion, a light band and no open preference (precedent, high).
